operations.description: Activates a pending recurring payment by creating the Solana subscriptions plan, authorizing the subscription, and storing the resulting on-chain identifiers and signatures. The source wallet gives the Subscriptions program's authority for that token an approval of 0, and each collection approves exactly its own amount in the same transaction as the pull, so the token program's `Approve` instruction appears in activation and collection transactions. If your custody provider's wallet policy allowlists programs or instructions, allow `Approve` to that authority, or the provider refuses the collection and SDP pauses the recurring payment with `pausedReason` `custody_policy_refused`.

operations.description: Refunds each leg to whoever deposited it and closes the trade. Unlike settlement this does not require the trade to be funded: unwinding a half-funded or abandoned trade is what it is for. Only the project's settlement authority can do this, and the action is irreversible. Refuses while another settle or cancel, or a funding or reclaim of either leg, is still in flight. The trade is recorded as cancelled only once the close is confirmed. Send an Idempotency-Key: a retry with the same key returns the signature of the close the first request sent instead of signing a second one. Requires only `dvp.manage`, not `dvp.execute`: cancelling is how a trade is unwound, and a key that can no longer execute must not leave both deposits in escrow until the trade expires.

operations.description: Permanently stops an active or paused recurring payment by submitting the Solana subscriptions immediate cancellation, which ends its on-chain subscription at once rather than at the end of the billing period. A canceled recurring payment never collects or resumes again. Every recurring payment from one wallet in one token relies on one token approval. When no other live recurring payment uses it, it is revoked right after the cancel; otherwise it stays for the schedules that still use it. The response's `tokenApproval` says which: `revoked`, `kept` with the recurring payments still using it in `sharedWith`, or `revoking` while a collection that was already processing settles, after which the background sweep revokes it. GET returns the same `tokenApproval` for a canceled recurring payment.

Optional, and honored when sent. 1-255 printable ASCII characters; send a UUID per logical operation and reuse it on every retry. Within 24 hours, a retry with the same key and the same request returns the stored status and body with the response header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Keys are scoped to the credential: within 24 hours, the same key with a different request, or from a different credential, returns 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; after that, the same key from a different credential runs as a new request. A rotated API key is a new credential, so after any rotation read the resource with GET to see whether the original request ran, and never resend a money request under the new credential without checking first. A key whose original request is still running returns 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` with `Retry-After`. A 400, 401, 403, 409 or 429 refusal is not stored, so the same key runs again once the cause is fixed. Access is checked before the key on every request, so a refused request never claims the key, and a credential that has since lost access to the named resource gets 403 instead of the stored response. A replay is a snapshot of the original response: read the current state with GET instead of sending the request again. If the original request never recorded its outcome (it crashed), a same-key retry gets 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` until 15 minutes plus the route's lease have passed since the original was sent (about 16 minutes, or about 20 for transfer batches), then 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` with no `Retry-After`, as does every later retry with that key: read the resource with GET to see whether it ran, then send again with a new key. A 5xx is stored and replayed like any other answer; retry it with a new key.

operations.description: Creates a delivery-versus-payment trade on chain and returns the escrow addresses to publish. Send an Idempotency-Key: a retry after an ambiguous broadcast returns the original trade, because without one the retry draws a fresh nonce and creates a SECOND trade at a different address while the first sits on chain with a published escrow nobody is watching. Creation requires no counterparty signature and commits neither leg's funds, so a created trade is a proposal rather than an agreement. It is also permissionless on chain — anyone can create a trade naming anyone, and the economic terms are not part of the account address, so whoever funds a leg must verify the stored terms first. Returns 403 when DvP is not enabled for the environment.

settlementDestination.description: Address the counter-leg proceeds are delivered to at settlement. funded.description: Whether the escrow holds at least the target amount. Settlement requires this on BOTH legs.

surplus.description: Amount held above the target, or null. Not harmless: settlement refunds the surplus to its depositor, and on a transfer-hook mint that refund can revert the whole settlement. Anyone can send tokens to an escrow, so a surplus is not rare.

frozen.description: Whether the escrow account is frozen. Funding transfers into a frozen escrow bounce, which a balance of zero cannot distinguish from nobody having paid yet.

funding.description: What the reconciler last observed in this escrow, or null before it has looked. Null is not zero.

fundingSignature.description: The transfer the calling organization sent into this leg's escrow, once it was broadcast. Null while that transfer is still being sent, for a leg funded by anyone else, and for an organization that did not fund it. Not a record of every deposit: the escrow accepts transfers from any address, and `transfers` lists them all.

outcome.description: Server-derived leg state: awaiting, partial, funded, overfunded, frozen, reclaimed, expired, delivered, refunded, recoverable after a late deposit, or closed without a recoverable balance. An open leg reads from its escrow balance against its amount, and reads reclaimed while the escrow's latest recorded transfer took tokens out and the balance is short of the amount.

direction.description: Into the escrow or out of it.

kind.description: What the movement was: a deposit into the escrow; a reclaim out of it before any close; the settlement's delivery or the cancellation's refund; a recovery of a late deposit after the close; or a withdrawal from a closed trade whose closing transaction is not among the transfers, which cannot be placed against the close.

operations.description: Verifies the signed bytes are exactly the built transaction and that every required signature is genuine (the owner's, and the fee payer's when the build named one), records the movement, then broadcasts. Requires the Idempotency-Key header: a retry with the same key resolves the original movement (`replayed: true`), and each built transaction is consumable exactly once. A build whose blockhash has expired is refused with 409 TRANSACTION_EXPIRED before anything is recorded; build again.

Idempotency key for safely retrying mutating requests. 1-255 printable ASCII characters; echoed back on the response.

transactionId.description: The built transaction being submitted; single-use.

signedTransaction.description: Base64 wire bytes of the signed transaction. They must be byte-for-byte the built message with only signatures added.

body.description: Submit the signed bytes back. Requires the Idempotency-Key header; a retry with the same key resolves the original movement instead of moving money twice.

status.description: Ledger vocabulary. `requested` means SDP recorded the signed transaction but has not yet confirmed it reached the network. `confirmed` is optimistic and can still be dropped by a fork; only `finalized` and `failed` are terminal.

settlement.description: Atomic transfers may show Done at confirmed while SDP tracks finality. Provider orders remain pending until fulfillment; chain confirmation alone is not payout. Older servers may omit this field; treat absent settlement semantics as unknown.

ownerAddress.description: The external wallet: the customer's own Solana address. It signs and owns the shares. It also pays the network fee unless an authenticated build names a `feePayer`. The pattern is necessary but not sufficient — the string must additionally decode to a 32-byte public key, which no pattern can express, so a well-shaped base58 string that does not decode still answers 400.

amount.description: Requested quantity, denominated in `denomination`.

denomination.description: Token mint for a deposit; share mint for a withdrawal.

tokenMint.description: The position's deposit-token mint. Render `tokenAmount` in these units; `amount`/`denomination` is the on-chain quantity (shares on a withdrawal).

tokenAmount.description: Quantity in `tokenMint` units. Kamino deposits and all withdrawals require a finalized observation; null beforehand or when the actual debit/payout cannot be observed. Other deposits report their fixed input amount.

replayed.description: True when the idempotency key already produced this movement and nothing was re-sent.

operations.description: Builds one unsigned vault deposit transaction for the wallet owner to sign. The build takes the provider entitlement, persists a submit-capable build, and may name a caller-controlled `feePayer` that signs alongside the owner. The transaction expires with its blockhash, and nothing moves during the build.

The pattern is necessary but not sufficient — the string must additionally decode to a 32-byte public key, which no pattern can express, so a well-shaped base58 string that does not decode still answers 400.

feePayer.description: Authenticated builds only: pay for this transaction from your own wallet instead of the customer's. The named address becomes the transaction's fee payer. It pays the network fee, funds any share-account rent, and must sign alongside the owner. Co-sign server-side with the fee payer's key before submitting. Simulation refuses the build with a 400 naming the fee payer when it cannot pay. Sending the owner's own address uses the default: the owner pays and signs alone.

amount.description: Deposit amount as a decimal string — the vault token's units, or the SOURCE token's units when `sourceTokenMint` requests a swap-funded build (the swap consumes it whole and the vault deposit is sized to the swap's guaranteed output).

minSharesOut.description: Slippage floor in share units. Required exactly when the selected strategy's `depositSlippage` is non-null. Derive it from `POST /v1/earn/deposits/preview`, never from the deposit amount.

sourceTokenMint.description: Fund the deposit in a different supported stablecoin (USDC, USDG, PYUSD or USDT on the environment's cluster): a Jupiter swap to the vault's own token is prepended inside the same transaction, so both legs land atomically or not at all. Equal to the strategy's deposit mint it is a no-op, so pickers may always send their selection.

swapSlippageBps.description: Swap slippage tolerance in basis points (default 2, accepted 1-500). Only valid together with sourceTokenMint. The deposit is sized to the swap's worst-case output, so a wider tolerance leaves a larger possible remainder of the vault token in the owner's account rather than risking the transaction.

body.description: Build one unsigned deposit transaction for an external wallet.

transaction.description: Base64 wire bytes of the UNSIGNED transaction for the external wallet to sign. It expires with its blockhash (about a minute).

sponsored.description: Whether SDP supplied and signed the fee payer. A partner-controlled feePayer leaves this false.

ownerAddress.description: The external wallet: the customer's own Solana address. It signs and owns the shares. It also pays the network fee unless an authenticated build names a `feePayer`. The pattern is necessary but not sufficient — the string must additionally decode to a 32-byte public key, which no pattern can express, so a well-shaped base58 string that does not decode still answers 400.

feePayer.description: Echo of an authenticated build request's `feePayer`. Present, this transaction requires the fee payer's signature IN ADDITION to the owner's — co-sign server-side before submitting; the submit refuses a missing or invalid fee-payer signature. Absent, the owner signs alone and pays the fee.

schema.description: Required for dashboard sessions. API keys use their assigned project.

Required: a request without one returns 400 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED`. 1-255 printable ASCII characters; send a UUID per logical operation and reuse it on every retry. Within 24 hours, a retry with the same key and the same request returns the stored status and body with the response header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Keys are scoped to the credential: within 24 hours, the same key with a different request, or from a different credential, returns 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; after that, the same key from a different credential runs as a new request. A rotated API key is a new credential, so after any rotation read the resource with GET to see whether the original request ran, and never resend a money request under the new credential without checking first. A key whose original request is still running returns 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` with `Retry-After`. A 400, 401, 403, 409 or 429 refusal is not stored, so the same key runs again once the cause is fixed. Access is checked before the key on every request, so a refused request never claims the key, and a credential that has since lost access to the named resource gets 403 instead of the stored response. A replay is a snapshot of the original response: read the current state with GET instead of sending the request again. If the original request never recorded its outcome (it crashed), a same-key retry gets 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` until 15 minutes plus the route's lease have passed since the original was sent (about 16 minutes, or about 20 for transfer batches), then takes over and is answered from the record it wrote. After a 5xx, a retry with the same key runs again and answers from the original record instead of acting twice; that answer also carries `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

operations.description: Executes an on-chain transfer using the exact SDP Wallet ID (`id` from `/v1/wallets`) and server-side signing through the connected provider. Requires an Idempotency-Key: a retry with the same key and request returns the original transfer instead of sending a second one. A 200 may return a processing transfer with its signature when broadcast or confirmation is still being reconciled; do not create a replacement transfer for that payment. A native SOL transfer is refused with 409 `AMOUNT_BELOW_RENT_MINIMUM`, before anything is written or sent, when it pays less than the rent-exempt minimum to an address with no account or would leave the source wallet holding more than nothing but less than the minimum.

operations.description: Executes an outbound transfer batch from one exact SDP Wallet ID, chunks recipients into Solana transactions, and returns the batch, recipient, and transfer records. Requires an Idempotency-Key: a retry with the same key and request returns the original batch without another on-chain submission. Recipient order does not change the request. A native SOL batch is refused with 409 `AMOUNT_BELOW_RENT_MINIMUM`, before anything is written or sent, when a recipient whose address has no account gets less than the rent-exempt minimum (`details.recipientIndexes`) or the source wallet would be left holding more than nothing but less than the minimum (`details.sourceRemainder`). A token batch is refused with 409 `SPONSORED_RENT_OVER_CAP` when one recipient's new token account costs more rent than the sponsor funds in a transaction (`details.recipientIndex`). An `externalId` already used by a batch on the same project and source wallet never pays again: the same request from the same credential returns that batch, and any other returns `409 TRANSFER_BATCH_RUN_EXISTS` with its `batchId` in `error.details`. To finish a batch after a partial failure, call `POST /v1/payments/transfer-batches/{batchId}/retry`: it sends only the batch's `failed` recipients. Never resend the whole batch under a new Idempotency-Key, which pays the recipients that succeeded again.

If the original request never recorded its outcome (it crashed), a same-key retry gets 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` until 15 minutes plus the route's lease have passed since the original was sent (about 16 minutes, or about 20 for transfer batches), then takes over and is answered from the record it wrote. Once the request has written its record, any answer below 500 is stored: a transfer that fails after that (such as 400 `TRANSACTION_FAILED` or a 409 signer mismatch) answers a same-key retry with the same error and `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, and after 24 hours the record answers with the same status and code. A 5xx is not stored: a same-key retry runs again and is answered from the record. To try again after a failure, send the request with a new key. After a 5xx, a retry with the same key runs again and answers from the original record instead of acting twice; that answer also carries `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

operations.summary: Create a deposit into the channel escrow
operations.description: Builds an escrow deposit from a connected wallet, requests signing through its provider, and broadcasts it to the instance chain (devnet), crediting `recipient` (defaults to the depositor) in the channel. Returns the deposit with its current status (submitted/confirmed, or failed). The credit (`credited`) is detected asynchronously via the gateway balance. Accepts a Clerk JWT or an API key. The source `walletId` must be a connected wallet enrolled under the project's Private Channels principal on this instance (and, for a wallet-scoped API key, one the key is bound to), and `recipient` must be an address verified on it. The `Idempotency-Key` header is REQUIRED: an identical retry returns the original deposit without a second escrow transfer, while reusing the key for a different request returns 409. New execution requires `private_channels.execute`, re-read at execution, authorization for one unambiguous source connected wallet, and runtime admission before signing setup or an SPC session. Every POST, including a matching replay, requires current `private_channels.execute` and authorization for the original source. A matching recorded result returns without a new signer or runtime admission; read-only access remains on the history GET endpoints. Separately authorized recovery of an abandoned operation may update its recorded state without a new provider signature.

operations.description: Provisions a new wallet under exactly one provider account: the project's Managed config for provider, or the Custody Connection named by connectionId. A body naming both, or neither, is rejected with 400. With an Idempotency-Key, SDP never records a second wallet for one key: a retry returns the wallet an earlier attempt recorded, including after the 24-hour key window. Privy and Coinbase CDP also receive a request id derived from the key, so they dedupe at the provider. A provider failure is stored as a 503, and a new key is a new provider request. A 503 can mean the provider created the wallet before the error, and with a provider other than Privy or Coinbase CDP, a failure that left no SDP wallet row makes even the same key a new provider request after 24 hours: before any retry after an ambiguous failure, whatever the key, check GET /v1/wallets and, if the wallet is not there, the provider account. The provider request id and the recorded-wallet lookup both include the credential, so after an API key rotation, once the key's 24-hour record has expired, the same key under the new credential is a new provider request and can create a second wallet: after a rotation, list wallets with GET /v1/wallets and check the provider account before retrying a create.

operations.summary: Fund your leg of a DvP trade
operations.description: Moves your side of the trade from its connected wallet into that leg's escrow. The counterparty needs nothing from this endpoint — they fund their own leg with an ordinary TransferChecked to the escrow address, which is the whole of their integration. The amount is the trade's, not a parameter: over-funding is a settlement risk, because settlement refunds the surplus and on a transfer-hook mint that refund can revert the whole settlement. Refuses a leg that is already funded, and refuses a frozen escrow with the reason rather than letting the transfer bounce; each refusal names its reason in error.details.reason. Send an Idempotency-Key: a retry with the same key returns the first request's result instead of funding again. Requires `dvp.execute`; a caller without it is refused with 403 INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS before anything is signed. The transfer runs immediately and only ever sends what is still outstanding.

The right to fund a side is holding an active connected wallet whose public key is that side's party address — derived at act time, never stored on the trade. An explicit walletId only narrows: it must hold the named side's address.

amount.description: Base units, as a string (u64). For fund, the shortfall sent. For reclaim, the escrow balance read before sending; the program returns whatever the escrow holds when it executes.

Defaults to `party` and may be set to a different address at create, which is ordinary for an execution desk settling into an account other than the one it funded from. Verify it before funding: creating a trade is permissionless and the terms are not bound by the trade's address, so a forged trade naming you can point its proceeds anywhere.

observedAmount.description: Raw base units last seen in the escrow, as a decimal string (u64).

funded.description: Whether the escrow holds at least the target amount. Settlement requires this on BOTH legs.

frozen.description: Whether the escrow account is frozen. Funding transfers into a frozen escrow bounce, which a balance of zero cannot distinguish from nobody having paid yet.

funding.description: What the reconciler last observed in this escrow, or null before it has looked. Null is not zero.

fundingSignature.description: The transfer the calling organization sent into this leg's escrow, once it was broadcast. Null while that transfer is still being sent, for a leg funded by anyone else, and for an organization that did not fund it. Not a record of every deposit: the escrow accepts transfers from any address, and `transfers` lists them all.

outcome.description: Server-derived leg state: awaiting, partial, funded, overfunded, frozen, reclaimed, expired, delivered, refunded, recoverable after a late deposit, or closed without a recoverable balance. An open leg reads from its escrow balance against its amount, and reads reclaimed while the escrow's latest recorded transfer took tokens out and the balance is short of the amount.

signature.description: The transaction that moved the tokens.

direction.description: Into the escrow or out of it.

kind.description: What the movement was: a deposit into the escrow; a reclaim out of it before any close; the settlement's delivery or the cancellation's refund; a recovery of a late deposit after the close; or a withdrawal from a closed trade whose closing transaction is not among the transfers, which cannot be placed against the close.

slot.description: Slot the transaction landed in, as a string (u64).

feePayer.description: The account that paid the transaction's fee.

transfers.description: Every recorded token movement in and out of this leg's escrow, oldest first. Filled by a background read of the escrow's history, so a transaction appears shortly after it confirms, not at once. A confirmed transaction the cluster later drops is removed. amount.description: Exact amount in base units, as a decimal string (u64).

escrow.description: Address to fund this leg. There is no funding instruction: a party funds by sending an ordinary TransferChecked of exactly `amount` to this address. Send exactly the amount — settlement refunds any surplus to the depositor, and on a transfer-hook mint that refund can revert the whole settlement.

settlementDestination.description: Address the counter-leg proceeds are delivered to at settlement. Defaults to `party` and may be set to a different address at create, which is ordinary for an execution desk settling into an account other than the one it funded from. Verify it before funding: creating a trade is permissionless and the terms are not bound by the trade's address, so a forged trade naming you can point its proceeds anywhere.

observedAmount.description: Raw base units last seen in the escrow, as a decimal string (u64).

funded.description: Whether the escrow holds at least the target amount. Settlement requires this on BOTH legs.

surplus.description: Amount held above the target, or null. Not harmless: settlement refunds the surplus to its depositor, and on a transfer-hook mint that refund can revert the whole settlement. Anyone can send tokens to an escrow, so a surplus is not rare.

frozen.description: Whether the escrow account is frozen. Funding transfers into a frozen escrow bounce, which a balance of zero cannot distinguish from nobody having paid yet.

funding.description: What the reconciler last observed in this escrow, or null before it has looked. Null is not zero.

fundingSignature.description: The transfer the calling organization sent into this leg's escrow, once it was broadcast. Null while that transfer is still being sent, for a leg funded by anyone else, and for an organization that did not fund it. Not a record of every deposit: the escrow accepts transfers from any address, and `transfers` lists them all.

outcome.description: Server-derived leg state: awaiting, partial, funded, overfunded, frozen, reclaimed, expired, delivered, refunded, recoverable after a late deposit, or closed without a recoverable balance. An open leg reads from its escrow balance against its amount, and reads reclaimed while the escrow's latest recorded transfer took tokens out and the balance is short of the amount.

signature.description: The transaction that moved the tokens.

direction.description: Into the escrow or out of it.

kind.description: What the movement was: a deposit into the escrow; a reclaim out of it before any close; the settlement's delivery or the cancellation's refund; a recovery of a late deposit after the close; or a withdrawal from a closed trade whose closing transaction is not among the transfers, which cannot be placed against the close.

amount.description: Base units moved, always positive, as a decimal string (u64).

slot.description: Slot the transaction landed in, as a string (u64).

blockTime.description: When the block was produced, or null when the cluster recorded no time.

feePayer.description: The account that paid the transaction's fee.

items.description: One token movement in or out of a leg's escrow, read off the chain from the escrow's balance before and after the transaction. Deposits from any address, settlement, cancellation and reclaims all appear here, whoever sent them.

transfers.description: Every recorded token movement in and out of this leg's escrow, oldest first. Filled by a background read of the escrow's history, so a transaction appears shortly after it confirms, not at once. A confirmed transaction the cluster later drops is removed. History before the trade was created is not read.

kind.description: The caller's standing on this trade, derived per caller and never stored. Display copy only: how many sides the caller holds an active connected wallet for — 0 is an agent trade (the terms were set for two other parties), 1 is a principal trade, 2 is bilateral. Follows the same wallet map discovery and funding authorize against, so a wallet-scoped key's kind reflects its own bindings.

nonce.description: Per-trade nonce, a decimal string (u64). Part of the PDA seeds, so it is never a JSON number.

expiryTimestamp.description: Unix seconds after which the trade can no longer settle, as a string (i64).

earliestSettlementTimestamp.description: Unix seconds before which settlement is refused, as a string (i64), or null.

settlementAvailability.description: Whether the trade can settle, judged by the cluster's Clock read with the last observation (the clock the program checks), never a host clock. `available`: both legs funded and inside the window. `unfunded`: a leg is short. `too_early`: funded, but before `earliestSettlementTimestamp`. `expired`: past expiry, only cancel or reclaim remain. Null for a closed trade, or a funded trade not yet observed with a cluster clock.

refString.description: Opaque client reference. Unauthenticated — anyone's trade can carry the same value, so treat it as a correlation hint and never as proof of origin.

createSignature.description: Signature of the transaction that created the trade.

observedAt.description: When the status was last confirmed against the chain.

operations.summary: Get one caller-signed wallet's balance and earnings
operations.description: Returns live balance and total earned per deposit token for the required `ownerAddress`: `earned` is live value plus observed withdrawal payouts (`totalWithdrawn`) minus finalized SDP deposits (`totalDeposited`), stated only when exact. When it cannot be stated (live value unavailable, movements still settling, or a finalized withdrawal whose payout was not observed) the figure is absent with a named reason, never zero. A wallet with no positions in the project's scope answers 200 with `positionCount: 0` and empty `totalsByToken`, never 404. Figures cover currently held positions: a fully exited position's history drops out (it stays on the movements list). Live value reads the owner's whole vault balance, so shares acquired outside SDP inflate it.

schema.description: Required for dashboard sessions. API keys use their assigned project.

ownerAddress.description: The external wallet: the customer's own Solana address. It signs and owns the shares. It also pays the network fee unless an authenticated build names a `feePayer`. The pattern is necessary but not sufficient — the string must additionally decode to a 32-byte public key, which no pattern can express, so a well-shaped base58 string that does not decode still answers 400.

unavailablePositionCount.description: Positions whose live value could not hydrate.

currentValue.description: Live value across the token's positions, including any par intermediate they hold. Absent when any contributing position is unavailable, so partial money is never presented as complete.

totalDeposited.description: Sum of observed finalized SDP deposits. Excludes unobserved receipts (see `deposits_not_valued`).

totalWithdrawn.description: Sum of the observed token payouts of finalized withdrawals, a ledger fact, always present. Excludes withdrawals whose payout was not observed (see `withdrawals_not_valued`).

earned.description: `currentValue + totalWithdrawn − totalDeposited`, stated only when exact and never coerced to zero. Live hydration reads the owner's whole vault balance, so shares acquired outside SDP inflate this figure.

earnedUnavailableReason.description: Why `earned` is absent: live value failed to hydrate; a movement is still settling; a held position has an open queued withdrawal request, whose shares leave the wallet before its payout (this can last days); or a held position has an unobserved finalized deposit or withdrawal, leaving `totalDeposited` or `totalWithdrawn` incomplete.

items.description: Earnings for one deposit token across the wallet's positions.

operations.description: Polls one recorded movement to a terminal state — the read that settles a submit whose outcome the caller never learned. Each poll observes the movement's exact signature on chain and advances the recorded status immediately, so state lands as fast as the network decides it; if the chain read is unavailable the last durable status is served and a background reconciler (about every minute) remains the recovery path. Keep polling until `finalized` or `failed` — those are the only terminal states.

status.description: Ledger vocabulary. `requested` means SDP recorded the signed transaction but has not yet confirmed it reached the network. `confirmed` is optimistic and can still be dropped by a fork; only `finalized` and `failed` are terminal.

Positions with an open queued withdrawal request are listed in `queuedWithdrawalPositions` instead.

unreadableWallets.description: Wallets whose balance read failed or ran out of the request budget. Their claims are unjudged in this report, never closed or marked unbacked.

A provider is available only when the deployment's release channel includes it, SDP currently offers it, the organization is entitled to it, and the deployment holds its credentials for the project's environment; the release channel offers the same providers to Sandbox and Production projects. Optional, and honored when sent. 1-255 printable ASCII characters; send a UUID per logical operation and reuse it on every retry. Within 24 hours, a retry with the same key and the same request returns the stored status and body with the response header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Keys are scoped to the credential: within 24 hours, the same key with a different request, or from a different credential, returns 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; after that, the same key from a different credential runs as a new request. A rotated API key is a new credential, so after any rotation read the resource with GET to see whether the original request ran, and never resend a money request under the new credential without checking first. A key whose original request is still running returns 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` with `Retry-After`. A 400, 401, 403, 409 or 429 refusal is not stored, so the same key runs again once the cause is fixed. Access is checked before the key on every request, so a refused request never claims the key, and a credential that has since lost access to the named resource gets 403 instead of the stored response. A replay is a snapshot of the original response: read the current state with GET instead of sending the request again. If the original request never recorded its outcome (it crashed), a same-key retry gets 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` until 15 minutes plus the route's lease have passed since the original was sent (about 16 minutes, or about 20 for transfer batches), then 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` with no `Retry-After`, as does every later retry with that key: read the resource with GET to see whether it ran, then send again with a new key. A 5xx is stored and replayed like any other answer; retry it with a new key.

operations.description: Lists the project's transactions across SDP modules with stable cursor pagination. Requires `transactions.read`. Every row also needs the `read` action of the module it comes from (which its `manage` or `execute` includes): a Payments row needs `transfers.read` for a transfer or deposit, `transfer_batches.read` for a batch item, `recurring.read` for a recurring collection, `payment_requests.read` for a payment request's fulfilment, and `onramp.read` or `offramp.read` for a ramp transfer; every other module's rows need that module's `read`. Rows the caller cannot read are left out. Requesting a module, or a Payments `kind`, without its action returns 403 INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS naming it. `search` matches transaction id, module id, or signature as a prefix, not a substring. The endpoint is metered (60/min per credential, 240/min per organization); exceeding the quota returns 429, and 503 indicates the quota backend was unavailable.

operations.summary: Reclaim your leg of a DvP trade
operations.description: Moves whatever your side's escrow holds back to the connected wallet at that side's party address, creating its token account first if needed. The trade stays open and the leg can be funded again. Works before and after expiry. Only the leg's own party can reclaim, so a counterparty's leg is theirs to pull back. Refuses a closed trade, an empty escrow, a leg whose funding is still in flight, and a transfer-hook mint; each refusal names its reason in error.details.reason. Send an Idempotency-Key: a retry with the same key returns the first request's result instead of reclaiming again. Requires only `dvp.manage`, not `dvp.execute`: this is the party's way back out of an escrow, and a key that can no longer fund must still be able to recover the deposit.

Optional, and honored when sent. 1-255 printable ASCII characters; send a UUID per logical operation and reuse it on every retry. Within 24 hours, a retry with the same key and the same request returns the stored status and body with the response header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Keys are scoped to the credential: within 24 hours, the same key with a different request, or from a different credential, returns 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; after that, the same key from a different credential runs as a new request. A rotated API key is a new credential, so after any rotation read the resource with GET to see whether the original request ran, and never resend a money request under the new credential without checking first. A key whose original request is still running returns 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` with `Retry-After`. A 400, 401, 403, 409 or 429 refusal is not stored, so the same key runs again once the cause is fixed. Access is checked before the key on every request, so a refused request never claims the key, and a credential that has since lost access to the named resource gets 403 instead of the stored response. A replay is a snapshot of the original response: read the current state with GET instead of sending the request again. If the original request never recorded its outcome (it crashed), a same-key retry gets 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` until 15 minutes plus the route's lease have passed since the original was sent (about 16 minutes, or about 20 for transfer batches), then 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` with no `Retry-After`, as does every later retry with that key: read the resource with GET to see whether it ran, then send again with a new key. operations.summary: Retry a transfer batch's failed recipients
operations.description: Sends the batch's `failed` recipients again, from the same source wallet with the batch's options, and no other recipient. A failed recipient was not paid: its transaction never reached the network or the network rejected it. Recipients still `pending` or `processing` may land and are never sent again. Each resent recipient keeps its row and links to its new chunk transfer. Takes no body and requires an Idempotency-Key: a retry with the same key sends nothing again: while its response is stored, it returns that saved response, and after a server error or once the response has expired, the batch as it stands. Read the batch's current state with `GET /v1/payments/transfer-batches/{batchId}`, and use a new key for each retry you mean to send. Any credential that may send from the batch's wallet can retry it. Each recipient is paid the address the batch recorded for it. Returns 409, sending nothing: `TRANSFER_BATCH_NOTHING_TO_RETRY` when the batch has no failed recipients (while it is `processing`, its unsent recipients become `failed` only once its request can no longer send them), `TRANSFER_BATCH_RETRY_CLAIMED` when a concurrent retry claimed them first, and `TRANSFER_BATCH_DESTINATION_CHANGED` (`details.recipientIds`) when a failed recipient's counterparty account has changed its address since (send that recipient in a new batch). A native SOL retry is refused with 409 `AMOUNT_BELOW_RENT_MINIMUM`, as create is, when a failed recipient would still be paid less than the rent-exempt minimum at an address with no account; its recipients stay `failed`. Only recipients that are still `failed` are ever sent, so a retry under a new key never pays anyone twice.

operations.description: Updates a recurring payment. Pending records are updated directly. Active metadata and due-date edits are applied in place, while active term, source, destination, or token edits create a replacement Solana subscription, authorize it, cancel the old subscription, and then swap the recurring payment to the replacement records. Requires an Idempotency-Key, because an edit can sign and broadcast a replacement subscription. A same-key retry of a completed edit replays its answer. A retry of an interrupted edit gets 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT with Retry-After until the attempt is stale, then resumes from the last step SDP recorded. If a step was sent but not yet recorded when the edit was interrupted, which is rare, the retry can fail or send that step again, so read the recurring payment with GET before editing it again.
